note: Exhausted by the end, and sweated a lot more than normal.
Lower back strain noticed the following day. Trap bar and Smith squat sets are the likely source; nothing was felt during the session itself.

First session back after two full rest days for the lower back strain, which was still present in the morning. Cable row was cut deliberately and pullups went to three sets to carry the pulling volume; the lat pulldown was kept because no chest-supported row was free. Two substitutions were forced by equipment rather than chosen: standing curls for preacher curls, and standing 15 lb Y raises for seated 20s. Both put the low back to work stabilising, which is the opposite of the intent -- worth watching against tomorrow's morning check-in. No sled, by plan, since it is tomorrow's session.

Sled only, by choice, on the fourth day after the lower-back strain and the first morning the back felt normal. Logged as "conditioning" because no program day is sled-only -- the sled is a 5-10 minute warmup or an optional finisher inside the four lifting days, never the session itself, so this will show as a deviation and should. Tiring and a heavy sweat despite no lifting, which is what fifty minutes at full resistance buys. The next lower session is being held back to Wednesday or Thursday rather than taken tomorrow.

A single full-body session by choice -- the only day this week training was possible -- covering the sled, jumps, trap bar, bench, pullups, squat and dips in one go. Typed "other" because no program day is full-body, so it draws no plan comparison and should read as the deviation it is. Performed order put pullups before the squat rather than after, which is the one departure from the plan that was not forced. The day's result is the trap bar: 260 for two sets of five, reported quite easy, eight days after the August 5 session at the same weight that the lower-back strain followed, and with nothing from the back this time. Bench was 150 rather than 155 only because the plates were not there. Pullups were reported quite hard, which is what taking them fifth in a full-body session five days after the last lifting day buys, and is not a reading on the path to ten. Upper traps flagged: reported as working hard on the trap bar, and reported as recurring.
